Sattar is a powerful film that stands out because of its strong performances and grounded storytelling. The movie keeps a serious tone and delivers its message clearly without unnecessary drama. The lead actor carries the film well, and the supporting cast adds depth to the narrative. The direction is focused, the screenplay is engaging, and the emotional moments feel natural rather than forced. Overall, Sattar is a meaningful and impactful watch that leaves a lasting impression and is worth recommending.

Good, excellent, i like it. The story follows Saad, a young man with a mundane job and a dream that's far from average - he wants to become a professional wrestler. Stuck in the daily grind of office life, Saad's life takes a twist when he decides to chase his childhood fantasy, setting off on a hilarious and chaotic journey to make his mark in the world of wrestling. To fulfill this wild dream, Saad crosses paths with shady trainers, makes odd friends, and deals with bizarre opponents in his quest to prove himself.

While the core story may appear simple, the film manages to balance laugh-out-loud comedy with inspiring character growth, giving the audience a protagonist to root for.
